$comment: This repo's adherence record against the shared knowledge library. `rules` are principles this repo has ADOPTED — each one enforced by a counted, ratcheting gate that fails `npm run check` when it rises. `declined` are principles reviewed and rejected FOR THIS REPO, each with a reason a later session can re-judge. Anything in library-index.json that appears in neither is UNREVIEWED, which check-library-adherence.mjs reports and never fails on. Every rule must cite a `principle` id that exists in the index; a gate with no grounding in the library is a gate nobody agreed to.

rules.verdictNote: PHYSICS: the library's clause — client state surviving a reload belongs behind one accessor, never bare storage calls scattered through components — landed here unchanged, and this repo had independently reached it (`useSchranka.ts:4` calls itself 'the only place that reads/writes localStorage', and handles the SSR case where the API does not exist). THIS REPO IS AHEAD ON THE SECOND HALF, and the library should adopt it: `followCodec.ts:25-26` puts the SCHEMA VERSION IN THE KEY (`politicas:schranka:v1`) so that a shape change becomes a new key and old data is simply never found. The library's principle only warns that a stored shape can drift from the code that reads it — crashing exactly the users who hold the old shape, and never the developer whose storage is already current. Version-in-the-key makes that class UNREPRESENTABLE with no migration code at all. That is a type-over-gate answer arrived at independently, and it is stronger than the advice it fulfils. This gate therefore enforces THIS REPO'S better pattern, not the library's generic one.
rules.title: Raw localStorage/sessionStorage access outside a typed persistence accessor

signal.description: A direct web-storage call OUTSIDE this repo's designated accessors. Measured 2026-08-14: 20 raw text occurrences, of which 13 are comment-only (the engine skips those — grep says 20, the engine says 7, and both are right about different questions). Of the 7 code sites, 2 are the accessor itself and are excluded below, leaving 5 across 2 files. Both remaining sites define their OWN storage key inside a component — `politicas.graph.variant` (GraphPage.tsx:40) and BALLOT_KEY (ReferendumPage.tsx) — and neither carries a schema version, so neither gets the protection `followCodec.ts` was written to provide. That is the precise drift this gate exists to stop: not 'someone used localStorage', but 'a second, unversioned key appeared outside the module that owns persistence'. PRECISION IS 100% BY CONSTRUCTION once the accessors are excluded — every surviving match is a component reaching past them. If a new accessor is added, exclude it here with a reason rather than raising the baseline.

exclude.reason: The designated accessor. Its own header says it is the only place that reads or writes localStorage, and it handles the SSR case where the API is absent — this is the destination the rule routes callers toward, not a violation.
Owns SCHRANKA_STORAGE_KEY and the version-in-the-key strategy this rule enforces. Excluding the module that defines the correct pattern is the same reasoning that exempts a token's own definition.

declined.reason: No Tauri IPC surface exists here — verified zero .rs files and no src-tauri directory. There is no command boundary to authorize.

Describes adding a #[tauri::command] and regenerating ts-rs bindings. This repo has no Rust and no IPC layer; its equivalent boundary is Next.js route handlers, which is a different situation the library has not yet written.
Concerns the flat global namespace of Tauri command wire keys. Next.js routes are namespaced by the filesystem, so the situation this principle exists to solve cannot arise here.
Specific to ts-rs generating TypeScript from Rust structs. There is no generated cross-language type boundary in this repo; types are authored once in TypeScript.
No Rust to test. This repo's equivalent lane is Vitest plus its own eslint-plugin rule tests, both already wired into npm run check.
Concerns cargo feature unification and per-feature compilation. There is no cargo build here; the analogous axis would be Next.js build-time env, which the library has not written as a principle.

Describes rusqlite row-to-Rust-struct mapping by column index and name. No rusqlite, no Rust structs. The general clause about positional mapping being fragile may still apply if this repo adds a SQL layer, so re-open this if scripts/gen-migration.ts grows into one.
